title: Paris nunciature (bishop of Bergamo, archbishop of Nazareth) to the Secretariat, 1585-86 (ASV Segr. Stato Francia 18; DECODE R15-R17)

documents.shelfmark: ASV Segr. Stato Francia 18/2, f. 206 (DECODE R16)

plaintext.source: No decifrato; DECODE's R16 decryption file is a copy of R15's.

transcription.notes: Used as found; not checked against the images.

documents.shelfmark: ASV Segr. Stato Francia 18/3, ff. 233-235 (DECODE R17)

system.summary: Two-digit homophonic cipher (second digit usually odd), null 8, marked 2-3 digit nomenclator codes.
system.sibling_key: DECODE D3103/D3105: Lasry's F18 key (Meister p. 324), used for R15
system.notes: R17 uses Meister no. 40 (variable-length, Morosini 1587), not the F18 key.

prior_solution.where: F18 key and an R15 decryption on DECODE (Lasry 2020); no R16 decryption

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R11-R17 record pages and DOC_ files with the session cookie.
Found R16's decryption file byte-identical to R15's (md5), so R16 was never decrypted.
Applied Lasry's F18 key to the DECODE transcription of R16: 1,410 pairs, 66 unknown, readable Italian on the 1586 alienation bull.
R17: DECODE F22 key is incomplete (full key in Meister p. 393) and its decryption file is a crash log.
Meister p. 324 no. 2 (Ragazzoni 1583 key with nomenclator) from OCR; realigned and added to the R16 decoder with a one-digit resync.
R17 decrypted with Meister p. 393 no. 40 via morosini1588/decrypt.py (LM beam search): all five pages, 5 unknown codes.

outcome.method_basis: R16 was read with Lasry's F18 key filed on the R15/R16 DECODE records (D3103/D3105); its nomenclator was added from Meister p. 324 no. 2 (Ragazzoni's 1583 Paris key), and R17 was read with Meister p. 393 no. 40, the key DECODE's own R17 note names; R15 had already been read by Lasry (2020).
outcome.fraction_read_source: R16_decryption.txt + R17_decryption.txt (scratchpad measure_A_units.py): units = plaintext letters (one per cipher pair) + one per bracketed code/name group; unread = every <..> group in R16 (unresolved codes and slips, 43 of 1,681) and [nnn?] codes in R17 (5 of 3,292). R16 0.974, R17 0.998. R15 (Lasry) not counted.
outcome.notes: R15 read before (Lasry); R16 read, 18 unknowns, names 18/48 unconfirmed; R17 read with Meister no. 40. fraction_read estimated from the notes (R16: 18 unknown of ~1,410 letter pairs after the Meister nomenclator; R17: 5 unknown codes; R15 read by Lasry), not measured token by token. Measured 21 Sept 2026: 0.99 of units read (R16 0.974, R17 0.998); codes_open = R16 codes 18 and 48 plus the five R17 codes (the other R16 <..> groups are mostly transcription slips).

gaps.detail: Meister's Ferrara/Parma values do not fit the contexts; the 1586 table may have moved them
unknowns after the one-digit resync; mostly transcription slips in TimB transcription D1610, images not re-read
Meister p. 393 no. 40 reads all five pages except 5 codes
